Cunda was a cruel pig butcher who cared not for the suffering he inflicted, and did no good deeds at all; before he died he started behaving like a pig himself, and later fell into Avīci, the hell of relentless suffering; the Buddha summarised the events with a verse.
Keywords: Killing, Wrong Livelihood, Retribution, Avīci, Animals

01-11.htm.title: 1.11 The Story about the Lay Disciple Dhammika
01-11.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Lay Disciple Dhammika together with further information.
01-11.htm.intro:
Dhammika, a good supporter, lay dying and he requested the bhikkhus to chant the Mindfulness discourse for him; seeing celestial chariots coming to take him away, he asked them to wait until the bhikkhus finished chanting, but the bhikkhus thought he was asking them to stop and go away; later the Buddha explained Dhammika was reborn in the Tusita Heaven and he spoke a verse about him.
Keywords: Offerings, Faith, Devatās, Heaven

01-12.htm.title: 1.12 The Story about Devadatta
01-12.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Devadatta together with further information.
01-12.htm.intro:
Devadatta grew jealous and plotted to kill the Buddha, when that failed he tried to cause a schism; eventually he wished to seek for forgiveness, but before he reached the Buddha he fell into Avīci, the hell of relentless suffering; the Buddha summarised the events with a verse.
Cast: Devadatta, Bhaddiya, Anuruddha, Ānanda, Bhagu, Kimbila, Mahānāma, Anuruddha (Annabhāra), Paccekabuddha Upariṭṭha, Upāli the Barber, Nālāgiri, Elder Sāriputta, Elder Mahā Moggallāna, Elder Kokālika
Keywords: Chief Disciples, Jealousy, Schism, Forgiveness, Bodhisatta, Devatās, Avīci

01-13.htm.title: 1.13 The Story about Queen Sumanā
01-13.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Queen Sumanā together with further information.
01-13.htm.intro:
The lay supporter Anāthapiṇḍika had three daughters; the youngest, after calling her father ‘younger brother’, died; the Buddha explained that Anāthapiṇḍika was her junior in the Dhamma, as she had attained the second stage of Awakening, and had been reborn in the Tusita Heaven, and he spoke a verse about her.
Cast: Visākhā, Anāthapiṇḍika, Mahā Subhaddā, Culla Subhaddā, Sumanā
Keywords: Offerings, Service, Death, Rich Men, Heaven

01-14.htm.title: 1.14 The Story about Two Monastic Friends
01-14.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Two Monastic Friends together with further information.
01-14.htm.intro:
Two friends ordained, one followed the path of practice and soon attained; the other the path of study and became puffed up with pride; the Buddha showed how the one who attained could answer his questions much better than the one who studied, and he spoke some verses about them.
Keywords: Pride, Devas, Recitation, Meditation

02-01.htm.title: 2.1 The Story about Udena
02-01.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Udena together with further information.
02-01.htm.intro:
King Udena had two queens, Sāmāvatī, who was a follower of the Buddha, and Māgandiyā, who was spurned by the Buddha; out of jealousy Māgandiyā brought about the destruction of Sāmāvatī and her five hundred followers, all of whom had attained stages of Awakening; Māgandiyā and her family, who were full of defilements, were put to death by the king; when what had happened was reported to the Buddha he spoke some verses about them.
Cast: King Allakappa, King Veṭhadīpaka, King Parantapa, Ghosaka, Kotūhalaka, Kāḷi, Kāpi, King Udena, Queen Sāmāvatī, Māgandiya, Queen Māgandiyā, Queen Vāsuladattā, Bhaddavatiya, Mitta, King Caṇḍa Pajjota, Kukkuṭa, Pāvāriya, Sumana, Khujjuttarā, Elder Ānanda
Keywords: Jealousy, Murder, Heedfulness, Offerings, Rich Men, Foremost Disciples, Epics, Past Lives, Reviling, Amanussa

02-02.htm.title: 2.2 The Story about Kumbhaghosaka
02-02.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Kumbhaghosaka together with further information.
02-02.htm.intro:
Kumbhaghosaka was a rich man’s son who escaped his afflicted household during a plague; later he disguised himself as a poor man and worked for his living, but was recognised by the king, who honoured him and gave him his daughter in marriage; when he heard the story the Buddha spoke a verse about him.
Cast: Kumbhaghosaka, King Bimbisāra
Keywords: Modesty, Riches, Honour

02-03.htm.title: 2.3 The Story about the Elder Culla Panthaka
02-03.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Culla Panthaka together with further information.
02-03.htm.intro:
When Elder Culla Panthaka could not remember even four lines of verse after three months trying, the Buddha asked him to rub a white cloth, which subsequently became soiled and gave him initial insight into impermanence; the Buddha then taught him that the mind is also defiled and must be cleansed, and he soon attained deliverance, after which the Buddha spoke a verse about him.
Cast: Culla Panthaka, Mahā Panthaka, Jīvaka Komārabhacca
Keywords: Insight, Skill in Means, Persistence, Rich Men, Foremost Disciples, Past Lives, Bodhisatta, Radiant Image, Previous Buddhas

02-04.htm.title: 2.4 The Story about the Fool’s Festival
02-04.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Fool’s Festival together with further information.
02-04.htm.intro:
During a seven-day festival of fools in Sāvatthī the people used to go round insulting and disrespecting everyone they met; the Buddha’s supporters asked him to stay at the monastery for the duration and they sent almsfood there; this is the teaching the Buddha gave them when it was over.
Keywords: Festivals, Foolish Talk

02-05.htm.title: 2.5 The Story about the Elder Mahā Kassapa
02-05.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Mahā Kassapa together with further information.
02-05.htm.intro:
Elder Mahā Kassapa, after collecting his almsfood, sat in meditation and tried to understand in all its breadth the rising and falling away of living beings; the Buddha advised him that only Buddhas have such thorough knowledge, and then he spoke a verse.
Keywords: Insight, Radiant Image, Foremost Disciples

02-06.htm.title: 2.6 The Story about Two Bhikkhu Friends, One Heedful and One Heedless
02-06.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Two Bhikkhu Friends, One Heedful and One Heedless together with further information.
02-06.htm.intro:
Two bhikkhus were given a meditation subject by the Buddha; one spent his time on monastic duties like sweeping, while the other was diligent and became an Arahat; after the Rains Retreat the Buddha commended the latter and spoke a verse about him.
Keywords: Heedfulness, Heedlessness, Hypocrisy, Meditation

02-07.htm.title: 2.7 The Story about Mahāli’s Questions
02-07.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Mahāli’s Questions together with further information.
02-07.htm.intro:
Prince Magha did good works in his village and inspired thirty-three others to join him; later they were reborn as Sakka and his company of Thirty-three; the Buddha spoke a verse explaining what had happened.
Cast: Mahāli, Sakka, Magha, Nandā, Cittā, Sudhammā, Sujātā, Vepacitti, Erāvaṇa, Vissakamma, Mātali
Keywords: Past Lives, Merit, Good Works, Heedfulness, Injustice, Loving-Kindness, Women, Asuras, Devas, Accharās, Cranes, Animals, Epics

02-08.htm.title: 2.8 The Story about a Certain Bhikkhu
02-08.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about a Certain Bhikkhu together with further information.
02-08.htm.intro:
A bhikkhu was given a meditation subject but could make no progress, so he determined to return to the Buddha; on his way he saw a great fire burn down a forest, and the Buddha appeared to him and taught him with a verse.
Keywords: Meditation, Heedfulness, Radiant Image

02-09.htm.title: 2.9 The Story about the Elder Nigamavāsī Tissa
02-09.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Nigamavāsī Tissa together with further information.
02-09.htm.intro:
Nigamavāsī Tissa lived near Sāvatthī and after he ordained he only went to his local village for alms; the bhikkhus blamed him but the Buddha praised him for being frugal and content, and spoke a verse praising his way of life.
Keywords: Frugality, Contentment, Animals, Sakka, Past Lives

03-01.htm.title: 3.1 The Story about Elder Meghiya
03-01.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Elder Meghiya together with further information.
03-01.htm.intro:
The Buddha’s attendant Meghiya left the Buddha alone against his wishes, and went and meditated in a mango grove; his mind was overcome with defilements and the Buddha taught him with some verses at the conclusion of which he attained Stream-entry.
Keywords: Wilfulness, Meditation

03-02.htm.title: 3.2 The Story about a Certain Bhikkhu
03-02.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about a Certain Bhikkhu together with further information.
03-02.htm.intro:
A female lay disciple supported some bhikkhus during the Rains Retreat and was given a meditation subject herself, with which she attained the third stage of Awakening; later a bhikkhu went to her and realised she knew his every thought, and was scared by that, but the Buddha told him to reside near her, and he taught him about the mind with a verse; soon he became an Arahat.
Cast: Mātika, Mātika’s mother
Keywords: Heedfulness, Solitude, Meditation, Mind-Reading

03-03.htm.title: 3.3 The Story about a Dissatisfied Bhikkhu
03-03.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about a Dissatisfied Bhikkhu together with further information.
03-03.htm.intro:
Anupubba was a faithful householder who fulfilled his duties to the monastics, and later was ordained himself, but became weary with all the rules and regulations; the Buddha told him his real duty was only to guard his mind, and further taught him with a verse.
Keywords: Faith, Discontent, Rich Men, Guarding the Mind

03-04.htm.title: 3.4 The Story about Nephew Saṅgharakkhita
03-04.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Nephew Saṅgharakkhita together with further information.
03-04.htm.intro:
Saṅgharakkhita ordained as a bhikkhu and received robes, one of which he wished to give to an elder, his uncle; the elder had no need for it though and refused it; Elder Saṅgharakkhita daydreamed about returning to the household life, and was distressed when his daydream was exposed, and the Buddha taught him in a verse.
Keywords: Discontent, Restraint

03-05.htm.title: 3.5 The Story about the Elder Cittahattha
03-05.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Cittahattha together with further information.
03-05.htm.intro:
Cittahattha wavered continually between being a bhikkhu and a householder, but eventually he saw into the truth of impermanence, ordained yet again and became an Arahat; the Buddha spoke some verses about him.
Keywords: Ordination, Impurity, Impermanence, Past Lives, Bodhisatta, Thieves

03-06.htm.title: 3.6 The Story about 500 Bhikkhus with Insight
03-06.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about 500 Bhikkhus with Insight together with further information.
03-06.htm.intro:
Five hundred bhikkhus were invited to stay in a forest for the Rains Retreat, but the Tree Devatās were not happy, and drove them away; the Buddha taught the bhikkhus the discourse about loving-kindness, they returned, and the Devatās served their needs; the bhikkhus developed insight and the Buddha then gave a teaching.
Keywords: Insight, Devatās, Protection Chanting, Loving-Kindness, Amanussa, Radiant Image

03-07.htm.title: 3.7 The Story about the Elder Pūtigatta Tissa
03-07.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Pūtigatta Tissa together with further information.
03-07.htm.intro:
Someone who had been a fowler in a previous life ordained, and became known as Elder Tissa, but not long after his body developed all kinds of sores; the Buddha washed his body, taught a verse and he became an Arahat, before dying for the last time.
Keywords: Diseases, Nursing, Insight, Past Lives, Previous Buddhas

03-08.htm.title: 3.8 The Story about Nanda the Herdsman
03-08.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Nanda the Herdsman together with further information.
03-08.htm.intro:
When the Buddha saw the cow-herder Nanda was ready he taught him the gradual path, and he attained Stream-entry, but shortly afterwards he was shot by a hunter and died; the Buddha then spoke a verse.
Keywords: Giving, Faith, Sudden Death

03-09.htm.title: 3.9 The Story about the Elder Soreyya
03-09.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Soreyya together with further information.
03-09.htm.intro:
A merchant’s son, Soreyya, developed lust for Elder Mahā Kaccāyana and was transformed into a woman; later, after asking pardon, he became a man again, ordained and soon became an Arahat; the Buddha explained what a well-directed mind can do for one.
Keywords: Sex Change, Rich Men, Solitude

04-01.htm.title: 4.1 The Story about 500 Bhikkhus Engaged in Talking about the Soil
04-01.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about 500 Bhikkhus Engaged in Talking about the Soil together with further information.
04-01.htm.intro:
Five hundred bhikkhus went on walkabout, and when they returned talked about the various kinds of earth they had seen; the Buddha told them to reflect on the earthiness in their own hearts, and spoke some verses.
Keywords: Similes

04-02.htm.title: 4.2 The Story about the Elder Who Meditated on a Mirage
04-02.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Who Meditated on a Mirage together with further information.
04-02.htm.intro:
A bhikkhu who had been practising meditation saw a mirage, and realised this was similar to existence; he next saw froth on a river, with its bubbles bursting, and he realised existence is the same; the Buddha summed up his insight with a verse.
Keywords: Meditation, Insight, Impermanence

04-03.htm.title: 4.3 The Story about Viḍūḍabha
04-03.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Viḍūḍabha together with further information.
04-03.htm.intro:
Prince Viḍūḍabha learned that he was the son of a Sakyan slave-woman due to a trick the Sakyans had played on his father, King Pasenadi, and he vowed revenge; on becoming king he massacred the Sakyans, but on his way home he and his army were swept away by flood waters; later the Buddha spoke a verse summarising what had happened.
Cast: Viḍūḍabha, Pasenadi, Mahāli, Bandhula, Visākhā, Suppavāsā, Sāriputta, Mahā Moggallāna, Ānanda, Kesava, Kappa, Nārada, Mahānāma, Vāsabhā Khattiyā, Mallikā, Dīgha Kārāyaṇa
Keywords: Chief Disciples, Slaves, Murder, Equanimity, Retribution, Epics, Past Lives

04-04.htm.title: 4.4 The Story about the One Who Honoured Her Husband
04-04.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the One Who Honoured Her Husband together with further information.
04-04.htm.intro:
Patipūjikā passed away from heaven and was reborn on earth, had four sons, served the monastics faithfully, and at the end of her life was reunited with her husband Mālabhārī in Tāvatiṁsa Heaven; the monastics told the Buddha about the loss of their benefactor, and he gave this teaching.
Keywords: Past Lives, Offerings, Heedlessness, Devaputtas, Accharās

04-05.htm.title: 4.5 The Story about the Selfish Kosiya
04-05.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Selfish Kosiya together with further information.
04-05.htm.intro:
Elder Moggallāna brought the miser Kosiya and his wife to the Buddha who taught them about generosity, and they both attained Stream-entry; the Buddha praised Elder Moggallāna for being both persuasive and modest with his supporters, and spoke a verse about him.
Keywords: Chief Disciples, Rich Men, Bodhisatta, Conversions

04-06.htm.title: 4.6 The Story about the Ājīvaka Pāṭhika
04-06.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Ājīvaka Pāṭhika together with further information.
04-06.htm.intro:
When a lay-disciple invited the Buddha for a meal, an ascetic supported by her abused both her and the Buddha, who advised her not to worry about what the ascetic is doing or saying but instead to look to herself; the Buddha then summarised his teaching with a verse.
Keywords: Ājīvakas, Offerings, Jealousy

04-07.htm.title: 4.7 The Story about the Lay Disciple Chattapāṇi
04-07.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Lay Disciple Chattapāṇi together with further information.
04-07.htm.intro:
When Elder Ānanda is sent to teach the two queens of King Pasenadi, Mallikā and Vāsabhā Khattiyā, the first profits by it but the latter does not; the Buddha explained why this was so with some verses.
Keywords: Non-returners, Kings, Queens, Listening to Dhamma

04-08.htm.title: 4.8 The Story about Visākhā
04-08.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Visākhā together with further information.
04-08.htm.intro:
Visākhā was a faithful supporter of the Buddha, but was married off to a son of Migāra, a supporter of the Jains; she insisted on inviting the Buddha for the wedding meal and Migāra was converted by his teaching; later she built the Eastern Monastery for the monastics; the Buddha spoke a verse to her.
Cast: Visākhā, Dhanañjaya, Sumanā Devī, Meṇḍaka, King Bimbisāra, King Pasenadi, Migāra, Puṇṇavaddhana, Elder Ānanda, Elder Mahā Moggallāna, Saṅghadāsī, King Kiki, Buddha Kassapa
Keywords: Rich Men, Kings, Marriages, Women, Monasteries, Foremost Disciples, Epics, Past Lives, Previous Buddhas

04-09.htm.title: 4.9 The Story about the Elder Ānanda’s Questions
04-09.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Ānanda’s Questions together with further information.
04-09.htm.intro:
When Elder Ānanda asked the Buddha if there is any fragrance that goes against the wind, the Buddha explained that if someone takes refuge, keeps precepts and is generous, the fragrance of his virtue will become widely known, and he spoke some verses.
Keywords: Giving, Foremost Disciples, Similes

04-10.htm.title: 4.10 The Story about Giving Alms to the Elder Mahā Kassapa
04-10.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Giving Alms to the Elder Mahā Kassapa together with further information.
04-10.htm.intro:
Elder Mahā Kassapa rose from meditation after seven days and went for alms; celestial spirits stepped forward to donate to him but he dismissed them, then Sakka and his wife Sujā disguised themselves as weavers and succeeded in giving alms, but Elder Mahā Kassapa discovered who they were and chided them; the Buddha spoke a verse about him.
Keywords: Accharās, Sakka, Devadhītās, Rich Men, Merit, Foremost Disciples

04-11.htm.title: 4.11 The Story about the Elder Godhika’s Parinibbāna
04-11.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Godhika’s Parinibbāna together with further information.
04-11.htm.intro:
Gravely ill, Elder Godhika kept falling away from his concentration and decided to commit suicide; after the event Māra searched high and low for his place of rebirth, but the Buddha asserted that he had not been reborn, and spoke a verse.
Keywords: Diseases, Suicide, Parinibbāna

04-12.htm.title: 4.12 The Story about Garahadinna
04-12.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Garahadinna together with further information.
04-12.htm.intro:
Sirigutta supported the Buddha, but his friend Garahadinna supported the Nigaṇṭhas; Sirigutta proved that the Nigaṇṭhas do not know the past, present and future as they declared; and the Buddha proved his knowledge and power to Garahadinna, who became his disciple; then the Buddha spoke some verses.
Keywords: Omniscience, Sectarians, Offerings, Wisdom, Rich Men, Conversions, Past Lives, Bodhisatta

05-01.htm.title: 5.1 The Story about a Certain Man
05-01.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about a Certain Man together with further information.
05-01.htm.intro:
King Pasenadi was overcome with desire for another man’s wife and sought to have him killed; during the night he woke to the sound of four people screaming; the Buddha explained they were adulterers in their previous lives and did no good deeds, and then he spoke a verse.
Cast: King Pasenadi Kosala, the elephant Puṇḍarīka, Queen Mallikā (Queen Dinnā), Buddha Kassapa, Sakka, King Uggasena
Keywords: Kings, Lust, Adultery, Killing, Epics, Past Lives, Previous Buddhas

05-02.htm.title: 5.2 The Story about the Elder Mahā Kassapa’s Pupil
05-02.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Mahā Kassapa’s Pupil together with further information.
05-02.htm.intro:
A faithless pupil of Elder Mahā Kassapa, after numerous other acts of deceit, tricked a supporter into giving him food and drinks which he said were needed by the elder; after being rebuked he burned down the elder’s hut, ran away and was later reborn in Avīci, the relentless hell; the Buddha then gave some advice in verse.
Keywords: Duties, Revenge, Foremost Disciples, Past Lives

05-03.htm.title: 5.3 The Story about the Rich Man Ānanda
05-03.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Rich Man Ānanda together with further information.
05-03.htm.intro:
The millionaire miser Ānanda was reborn in great poverty and distress, and had to beg for his meals; he returned to his previous home, but was thrown out by his son; the Buddha then asked Ānanda to show his son where he buried his gold, and his son converted; the Buddha then spoke a verse.
Cast: The Rich Man Ānanda, his son Mūlasiri
Keywords: Selfishness, Rich Men, Past Lives

05-04.htm.title: 5.4 The Story about the Thieves Who Broke Their Bonds
05-04.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Thieves Who Broke Their Bonds together with further information.
05-04.htm.intro:
Two thieves went to listen to the Dhamma; one of them attained a stage of Awakening, the other managed to undo a knot in someone’s clothes and steal some pennies; when this was reported to the Buddha he spoke a verse in explanation.
Keywords: Thieves, Listening to Dhamma

05-05.htm.title: 5.5 The Story about the Elder Udāyī
05-05.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Udāyī together with further information.
05-05.htm.intro:
Elder Udāyī lived with the Buddha, but when questioned by visiting bhikkhus it was found he did not know even the fundamentals of the teaching; they told this to the Buddha, who spoke a verse.
Keywords: Fools, Wisdom

05-06.htm.title: 5.6 The Story about 30 Bhikkhus from Pāṭheyya
05-06.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about 30 Bhikkhus from Pāṭheyya together with further information.
05-06.htm.intro:
The thirty youths from Pāṭheyyaka were amongst the Buddha’s first converts; later he taught them about the impossibility of knowing the beginning of the rounds of births and deaths, and they immediately became Arahats; the Buddha spoke a verse about them.
Keywords: Insight

05-07.htm.title: 5.7 The Story about the Leper Suppabuddha
05-07.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Leper Suppabuddha together with further information.
05-07.htm.intro:
The leper Suppabuddha heard the Dhamma and attained Stream-entry, but was killed by a cow soon after, and was reborn in heaven; the Buddha explained that together with three others, he had killed a cow in a previous existence, and that the cow had vowed revenge; the Buddha then spoke a verse.
Cast: Suppabuddha, Sakka, Pukkusāti, Bāhiya Dārucīriya, Tambadāṭhika, Paccekabuddha Tagarasikhi
Keywords: Treasures, Yakkhinīs, Killing, Past Lives

05-08.htm.title: 5.8 The Story about a Farmer
05-08.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about a Farmer together with further information.
05-08.htm.intro:
The Buddha warned a farmer regarding a thousand gold coins dropped by a thief in his field; the farmer covered them over and continued ploughing; some people investigating the robbery traced the thieves to his field and uncovered the coins and he was arrested; the Buddha affirmed the farmer’s innocence and spoke a verse.
Cast: The Farmer, Elder Ānanda
Keywords: Thieves, Rich Men, Kings

05-09.htm.title: 5.9 The Story about Sumana the Garland-Maker
05-09.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Sumana the Garland-Maker together with further information.
05-09.htm.intro:
The flower seller Sumana delivered flowers to the king each day, but one day when he saw the Buddha he sprinkled the flowers over him, and they remained in the air around the Buddha and the whole city came out to see the spectacle; the Buddha predicted Sumana would never go to the lower worlds again and one day would become a Paccekabuddha, and spoke a verse in praise of his action.
Cast: The Garland-Maker Sumana, King Bimbisāra, Elder Ānanda
Keywords: Offerings, Kings

05-10.htm.title: 5.10 The Story about the Elder Uppalavaṇṇā
05-10.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Uppalavaṇṇā together with further information.
05-10.htm.intro:
A cousin of the bhikkhunī Elder Uppalavaṇṇā hid in her forest dwelling and raped her when she returned; later the earth swallowed him up and he was reborn in Avīci, the relentless hell; the Buddha then gave a teaching.
Cast: Uppalavaṇṇā, her cousin Ānanda, King Pasenadi
Keywords: Bhikkhunīs, Insight, Sexual Misconduct

05-11.htm.title: 5.11 The Story about the Ājīvaka Jambuka
05-11.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Ājīvaka Jambuka together with further information.
05-11.htm.intro:
For many years the Ājīvaka Jambuka ate excrement and slept on the floor yet convinced his devotees that he only ate food from a grass-tip and never slept, until the Buddha confronted him with his deceit; Jambuka repented, ordained and soon became an Arahat; the Buddha spoke a verse to Jambuka’s devotees.
Cast: Jambuka, Buddha Kassapa, Elder Ānanda, Four Great Kings, Sakka, Mahā Brahma
Keywords: Jealousy, Ascetics, Demerit, Past Lives, Previous Buddhas

05-12.htm.title: 5.12 The Story about the Snake Peta
05-12.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Snake Peta together with further information.
05-12.htm.intro:
A man burned down the hut of a Paccekabuddha and eventually was reborn as a snake Peta, burning for the whole length of his long body, as was seen by Elder Moggallāna; the Buddha confirmed the story, and gave a teaching.
Cast: Elder Lakkhaṇa, Elder Mahā Moggallāna, Buddha Kassapa
Keywords: Chief Disciples, Petas, Avīci, Past Lives, Previous Buddhas

05-13.htm.title: 5.13 The Story about the Peta with Sixty Hammers
05-13.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Peta with Sixty Hammers together with further information.
05-13.htm.intro:
A young man learned the art of stone-throwing, but used it to kill a Paccekabuddha; he was reborn in Avīci, the hell of relentless suffering, and later as a Peta whose head was constantly crushed by sixty hammers; the Buddha explained what happens to fools who gain knowledge with a verse.
Cast: Elder Lakkhaṇa, Elder Mahā Moggallāna, Paccekabuddha Sunetta
Keywords: Chief Disciples, Skill, Killing, Past Lives

05-14.htm.title: 5.14 The Story about the Edler Sudhamma
05-14.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Edler Sudhamma together with further information.
05-14.htm.intro:
The householder Citta sought to give alms to the two chief disciples, but the jealous resident bhikkhu Elder Sudhamma felt offended and refused to attend; the Buddha admonished him with some verses and he soon became an Arahat.
Cast: Householder Citta, Elder Mahānāma, Elder Sudhamma, Elder Sāriputta, Elder Mahā Moggallāna, Elder Ānanda, Buddha Padumuttara, Buddha Kassapa
Keywords: Offerings, Listening to Dhamma, Jealousy, Pride, Faith, Rich Men, Chief Disciples, Devatās, Past Lives, Previous Buddhas

05-15.htm.title: 5.15 The Story about the Elder Vanavāsī Tissa
05-15.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Vanavāsī Tissa together with further information.
05-15.htm.intro:
The seven year old boy Tissa ordained under Elder Sāriputta, and later, spurning gains and the attentions of his relatives, went forth into solitude, and quickly became an Arahat; the Buddha spoke a verse about him.
Cast: Elder Sāriputta, Brahmin Mahāsena, Brahmin Vaṅganta, Vanavāsī Tissa (Piṇḍapātadāyaka Tissa, Kambaladāyaka Tissa), Brahmin Mahāsena, Elder Sāriputta, Elder Mahā Moggallāna, Upasāḷhaka, Elder Ānanda
Keywords: Offerings, Past Lives, Novices, Chief Disciples, Bodhisatta, Death

06-01.htm.title: 6.1 The Story about the Elder Rādha
06-01.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Rādha together with further information.
06-01.htm.intro:
The bhikkhus did not want to ordain a poor Brahmin, Rādha, but the Buddha, seeing his potential, allowed it; Elder Sāriputta gave him guidance which he followed to the letter and soon became an Arahat; the Buddha then spoke a verse about being amenable to admonition.
Keywords: Chief Disciples, Kings, Bodhisatta, Animals

06-02.htm.title: 6.2 The Story about the Followers of Assaji and Punabbasu
06-02.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Followers of Assaji and Punabbasu together with further information.
06-02.htm.intro: The Buddha asked the Chief Disciples to advise and instruct some of their wayward disciples; some accepted the advice, some returned to lay life, and others were later expelled; the Buddha spoke a verse by way of instruction.

06-03.htm.title: 6.3 The Story about the Elder Channa
06-03.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Channa together with further information.
06-03.htm.intro:
Elder Channa was always abusing the Chief Disciples; when the Buddha found out he admonished him with a verse, but still he refused to refrain; at the Buddha’s bidding he was isolated by the bhikkhus. He later repented and became an Arahat.
Cast: Channa, Elder Sāriputta, Elder Mahā Moggallāna
Keywords: Chief Disciples, Reviling, Punishment

06-04.htm.title: 6.4 The Story about the Elder Mahā Kappina
06-04.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Mahā Kappina together with further information.
06-04.htm.intro:
Elder Mahā Kappina, who was formerly a king, was given to exclaiming his delight, and the bhikkhus feared he was recalling the joys he had when king; the Buddha explained the true reason for his exclamations was delight in the Dhamma, and spoke a verse about him.
Cast: Buddha Padumuttara, Buddha Kassapa, Mahā Kappina, Queen Anojā,
Keywords: Foremost Disciples, Merit, Devaputtas, Offerings, Past Lives, Renunciation, Previous Buddhas

06-05.htm.title: 6.5 The Story about the Novice Paṇḍita
06-05.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Novice Paṇḍita together with further information.
06-05.htm.intro:
The novice Paṇḍita saw that irrigators, fletchers and carpenters mastered the objects they worked with, and realised that if they can master unconscious things, he could master his mind; by striving he did just that and became an Arahat; the Buddha then spoke a verse about him.
Cast: Novice Paṇḍita, Buddha Kassapa, Sakka, Four Great Kings, Mahā Duggata, Elder Sāriputta
Keywords: Novices, Generosity, Poverty, Rich Men, Pregnancy, Mastery, Past Lives, Previous Buddhas

06-06.htm.title: 6.6 The Story about the Elder Lakuṇṭaka Bhaddiya
06-06.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Lakuṇṭaka Bhaddiya together with further information.
06-06.htm.intro:
The Elder Lakuṇṭaka Bhaddiya was a dwarf who became an Arahat; because of his condition the novices and others used to tease him, but he remained unmoved and the Buddha explained why this was so with a verse.
Keywords: Novices, Teasing, Equanimity

06-07.htm.title: 6.7 The Story about the Mother of Kāṇā
06-07.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Mother of Kāṇā together with further information.
06-07.htm.intro:
Kāṇā resented and reviled the bhikkhus for taking cakes she wanted to offer to her husband; but the Buddha showed they had only taken what was offered, and she gained faith and attained Stream-entry; the Buddha explained she had also been offended in a past life, and then spoke a verse.
Keywords: Offerings, Marriages, Reviling, Kings, Animals, Past Lives, Bodhisatta

06-08.htm.title: 6.8 The Story about Five Hundred Bhikkhus
06-08.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Five Hundred Bhikkhus together with further information.
06-08.htm.intro:
During a famine the Buddha and his bhikkhus lived frugally and without complaint; later rogues who lived off the leftovers of the bhikkhus roamed around making a nuisance of themselves; the Buddha praised those who live restrained and spoke a verse.
Cast: Brahmin Verañjā, Māra, Elder Mahā Moggallāna
Keywords: Chief Disciples, Greed, Laziness, Past Lives, Strong Drink

06-09.htm.title: 6.9 The Story about the Elder Dhammika
06-09.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Dhammika together with further information.
06-09.htm.intro:
The householder Dhammika wanted to ordain, but his wife persuaded him for some time to delay it; eventually he ordained anyway, became an Arahat, and went back to teach his wife and son, who themselves ordained and became Arahats; the Buddha taught a verse with Elder Dhammika in mind.
Keywords: Renunciation, Families

06-10.htm.title: 6.10 The Story about Listening to the Dhamma
06-10.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Listening to the Dhamma together with further information.
06-10.htm.intro:
Some people in Sāvatthī went to listen to Dhamma, but were overcome by lust, hatred or drowsiness, and none of them gained from it; the Buddha explained that this is quite common amongst people with a verse.
Keywords: Pollutants, Listening to Dhamma

06-11.htm.title: 6.11 The Story about Five Hundred Visiting Bhikkhus
06-11.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Five Hundred Visiting Bhikkhus together with further information.
06-11.htm.intro:
Fifty bhikkhus who passed the Rains Retreat in Kosala visited the Buddha in Sāvatthī after the Retreat and this is the inspiring teaching the Buddha gave them on that occasion.
Keywords: Renunciation, Monastics

07-01.htm.title: 7.1 The Story about Jīvaka’s Question
07-01.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Jīvaka’s Question together with further information.
07-01.htm.intro:
Devadatta hurled a rock down on the Buddha, which cut his foot; the Buddha’s physician Jīvaka applied medicine which needs to be applied for only a short time, but immediately thereafter he had to leave and was unable to return; the Buddha knew his thoughts though and asked Elder Ānanda to remove the medicine; the next day Jīvaka asked if the Buddha suffered pain because of his oversight, and the Buddha gave his reply in a verse.
Cast: Jīvaka, Elder Ānanda, Devadatta, Prince Ajātasattu
Keywords: Doctors, Medicine

07-02.htm.title: 7.2 The Story about the Elder Mahā Kassapa
07-02.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Mahā Kassapa together with further information.
07-02.htm.intro:
The Buddha set out on walkabout with a great host of bhikkhus, but seeing none left behind in Sāvatthī, he sent Elder Mahā Kassapa and his entourage back; some bhikkhus, not knowing about the instruction, accused the elder of being attached to his regular supporters, but the Buddha explained it was otherwise.
Keywords: Walkabout, Obedience, Great Disciples

07-03.htm.title: 7.3 The Story about the Elder Belaṭṭhisīsa
07-03.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Belaṭṭhisīsa together with further information.
07-03.htm.intro:
Elder Belaṭṭhisīsa took to storing up food so as not to be bothered with the almsround; the bhikkhus reported it to the Buddha, who laid down a rule forbidding the storing of food, and gave this teaching.
Keywords: Offerings, Discipline

07-04.htm.title: 7.4 The Story about the Elder Anuruddha
07-04.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Anuruddha together with further information.
07-04.htm.intro:
The Buddha and the bhikkhus gathered round to help make a robe for Elder Anuruddha; a former relative of his, who was then a Devadhītā, incited the villagers to give alms, which they did, but the bhikkhus suspected Elder Anuruddha gave the order for a great alms feast; the Buddha reproved them with a verse.
Cast: Elder Anuruddha, Devadhītā Jālinī, Elder Mahā Kassapa, Elder Sāriputta, Elder Ānanda, Elder Mahā Moggallāna, Sakka
Keywords: Chief Disciples, Offerings, Discipline

07-05.htm.title: 7.5 The Story about the Elder Mahā Kaccāyana
07-05.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Mahā Kaccāyana together with further information.
07-05.htm.intro:
Elder Mahā Kaccāyana, even though he lived far away, would regularly come to hear the Buddha teach; one day Sakka saw the elder was absent and wished he would come, and suddenly he appeared; Sakka paid homage to him and the Buddha recited a verse.
Keywords: Great Disciples, Respect, Offerings

07-06.htm.title: 7.6 The Story about the Elder Sāriputta
07-06.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Sāriputta together with further information.
07-06.htm.intro:
Elder Sāriputta is slandered by one of the bhikkhus, and the Buddha called him to account for himself; instead of defending himself he enumerated his virtues, which caused the great earth to quake; the bhikkhu who slandered him then asked pardon and Elder Sāriputta asked pardon in return; the Buddha then spoke a verse.
Keywords: Chief Disciples, Grudges, Slander, Lion’s Roar, Similes

07-07.htm.title: 7.7 The Story about Kosambivāsī Tissa’s Novice
07-07.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Kosambivāsī Tissa’s Novice together with further information.
07-07.htm.intro:
Elder Tissa ordained a novice, who in the ordination hall became an Arahat; later they travelled, and through the carelessness of the bhikkhu the novice’s eye was put out; the novice, however, didn’t get angry but went about his duties as normal; the Buddha explained it with a verse.
Keywords: Novices, Injuries, Forgiveness

07-08.htm.title: 7.8 The Story about the Question and Answer to the Elder Sāriputta
07-08.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Question and Answer to the Elder Sāriputta together with further information.
07-08.htm.intro:
Elder Sāriputta, when questioned by the Buddha, declared he didn’t have faith simply through listening to others, implying he has seen for himself; other bhikkhus thought he has said he didn’t have faith in the Buddha, so the latter taught a verse to explain the situation.
Keywords: Great Disciples, Faith

07-09.htm.title: 7.9 The Story about the Elder Khadiravaniya Revata
07-09.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Khadiravaniya Revata together with further information.
07-09.htm.intro:
Elder Sāriputta’s youngest brother Revata escaped from the household life, ordained, and soon after became an Arahat; after the Rains Retreat the Buddha visited him, and by spiritual power he transformed the thorn thickets he lived in into something well-equipped and quite delightful; when two old bhikkhus returned they found only a thorn thicket; the Buddha explained how it is so.
Cast: Elder Khadiravaniya Revata, Elder Sāriputta, Elder Cālā, Elder Upacālā, Elder Sīsūpacālā, Elder Canda, Elder Upasena, Elder Ānanda, Elder Sīvali, Visākhā, Buddha Vipassī
Keywords: Old Age, Great Disciples, Marriages, Discipline, Kings, Offerings, Gifts Beyond Compare, Past Lives, Avīci, Amanussa

07-10.htm.title: 7.10 The Story about a Certain Woman
07-10.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about a Certain Woman together with further information.
07-10.htm.intro:
A courtesan came across a meditating bhikkhu in the wilderness and sought to seduce him by stripping and flirting with him, when he saw her he became excited; the Buddha sent forth his image and gave the bhikkhu this advice.
Keywords: Passion, Women, Seclusion, Radiant Image

08-01.htm.title: 8.1 The Story about the Copper-Toothed Executioner
08-01.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Copper-Toothed Executioner together with further information.
08-01.htm.intro:
A man worked all his life as a public executioner and later had deep regret about his actions; Elder Sāriputta gave him just one teaching and he was reborn in Tusita Heaven; the bhikkhus wondered how this could be, and the Buddha spoke a verse to explain it.
Keywords: Past Deeds, Forgiveness, Listening to Dhamma, Yakkhinīs, Heaven

08-02.htm.title: 8.2 The Story about the Elder Bāhiya Dārucīriya
08-02.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Bāhiya Dārucīriya together with further information.
08-02.htm.intro:
Bāhiya Dārucīriya obtained a short teaching from the Buddha, became an Arahat and died straight afterwards; the Buddha appointed him as foremost amongst those who were quick to grasp the teaching, and when the bhikkhus doubted it, he taught them with a verse.
Cast: Bāhiya Dārucīriya, Buddha Kassapa, King Pukkusāti, Elder Kumāra Kassapa, Dabba the Malla, Elder Sabhiya
Keywords: Ascetics, Devatās, Past Lives, Yakkhinīs, Foremost Disciples, Previous Buddhas

08-03.htm.title: 8.3 The Story about the Elder Kuṇḍalakesī
08-03.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Kuṇḍalakesī together with further information.
08-03.htm.intro:
Kuṇḍalakesī, who had previously killed her husband and joined the wanderers and expertly defended their doctrines, was converted by Elder Sāriputta with a simple teaching; the bhikkhus wondered how, and the Buddha spoke some verses to explain it.
Keywords: Marriages, Thieves, Wanderers, Women, Bhikkhunīs, Debates

08-04.htm.title: 8.4 The Story about the Brahmin Who Asked about Loss
08-04.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Brahmin Who Asked about Loss together with further information.
08-04.htm.intro:
A Brahmin admitted to earning his living through gambling, and the Buddha explained that gains in this way are no true gains, but those who overcame themselves are truly victorious, and then he gave him a teaching.
Keywords: Self-Conquest

08-05.htm.title: 8.5 The Story about the Elder Sāriputta’s Brahmin Uncle
08-05.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Sāriputta’s Brahmin Uncle together with further information.
08-05.htm.intro:
Elder Sāriputta asked the Buddha to teach his uncle, who supported the Nigaṇṭhas, the true way to the Brahma world; and the Buddha spoke a verse with which he taught them.
Keywords: Offerings, Worship, Great Disciples

08-06.htm.title: 8.6 The Story about the Elder Sāriputta’s Nephew
08-06.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Sāriputta’s Nephew together with further information.
08-06.htm.intro:
Elder Sāriputta asked the Buddha to teach his nephew, who slayed animals and tended the sacrificial fire, the true way to the Brahma world, and the Buddha gave a teaching in a verse.
Keywords: Sacrifice, Worship, Great Disciples

08-07.htm.title: 8.7 The Story about the Elder Sāriputta’s Brahmin Companion
08-07.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Sāriputta’s Brahmin Companion together with further information.
08-07.htm.intro:
Elder Sāriputta asked the Buddha to teach his friend, who offered animals in sacrifice, the true way to the Brahma world, and the Buddha gave him a teaching in a verse.
Keywords: Sacrifice, Worship, Great Disciples

08-08.htm.title: 8.8 The Story about the Youth Dīghāyu
08-08.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Youth Dīghāyu together with further information.
08-08.htm.intro:
When the boy Dīghāyu was destined to die, the Buddha and the bhikkhus chanted protective verses for him and he lived on; the Buddha said long life is not the only thing a man received when he reverenced the elders, and then he taught them with a verse.
Keywords: Protection Chanting, Longevity, Devatās

08-09.htm.title: 8.9 The Story about the Novice Saṅkicca
08-09.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Novice Saṅkicca together with further information.
08-09.htm.intro:
Elder Sāriputta’s nephew Saṅkicca ordained as a novice, and when thirty bhikkhus’ lives were threatened by five hundred thieves he converted the thieves and they ordained; when he heard about it, this is the teaching the Buddha gave.
Cast: Elder Sāriputta, Novice Saṅkicca, Novice Atimuttaka
Keywords: Novices, Solitude, Meditation, Rich Men, Thieves, Devatās, Conversions

08-10.htm.title: 8.10 The Story about the Elder Khāṇu Koṇḍañña
08-10.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Khāṇu Koṇḍañña together with further information.
08-10.htm.intro:
Elder Khāṇu Koṇḍañña, sitting in meditation, was unmoved when five hundred thieves piled up their stolen goods all over him at night; the thieves, impressed with his equanimity, converted and were ordained; the Buddha gave a teaching in a verse on that occasion.
Keywords: Thieves, Conversions, Amanussa

08-11.htm.title: 8.11 The Story about the Elder Sappadāsa
08-11.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Sappadāsa together with further information.
08-11.htm.intro:
Elder Sappadāsa was dissatisfied and thought to end his life, but became an Arahat with the razor at his windpipe; when questioned by the bhikkhus the Buddha explained that one who truly strives can attain Awakening in an instant, and he spoke a verse.
Cast: Elder Sappadāsa, Buddha Kassapa
Keywords: Discontent, Suicide, Past Lives, Previous Buddhas

08-12.htm.title: 8.12 The Story about the Elder Paṭācārā
08-12.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Paṭācārā together with further information.
08-12.htm.intro:
Paṭācārā ran away from home with one of her slaves, had two children and lost them both, along with her husband, parents and brother in one day; she went mad and by and by approached the Buddha who, recognising she was ready for Awakening, taught her about the endless sorrow of births and deaths, and then spoke a verse hearing which she became an Arahat.
Keywords: Women, Marriages, Death, Grief, Madness, Ordination, Insight, Radiant Image, Foremost Disciples

08-13.htm.title: 8.13 The Story about Kisā Gotamī
08-13.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Kisā Gotamī together with further information.
08-13.htm.intro:
When Kisā Gotamī sought medicine for her dead son, the Buddha asked her to bring mustard seeds from a house that has never seen death; she learned during her quest that everyone dies, and the Buddha taught her further with a verse.
Keywords: Riches, Poverty, Death, Ordination, Insight, Radiant Image, Foremost Disciples

08-14.htm.title: 8.14 The Story about the Elder Bahuputtikā
08-14.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Bahuputtikā together with further information.
08-14.htm.intro:
A good lay disciple, Bahuputtikā, was despised by her children and decided to ordain and was very resolute in her practice; the Buddha gave this teaching and she attained Awakening.
Keywords: Wealth, Ordination, Meditation, Radiant Image, Foremost Disciples

09-01.htm.title: 9.1 The Story about the Brahmin Culla Ekasāṭaka
09-01.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Brahmin Culla Ekasāṭaka together with further information.
09-01.htm.intro:
A Brahmin had only one cloak, and hesitated to give it to the Buddha, but eventually in the last watch of the night he did give it, and he was richly rewarded by the king; the Buddha explained his reward would have been greater had he not hesitated, and spoke a verse.
Cast: Buddha Vipassī, Mahā Ekasāṭaka, Culla Ekasāṭaka
Keywords: Listening to Dhamma, Offerings, Kings, Gift of Fours

09-02.htm.title: 9.2 The Story about the Elder Seyyasaka
09-02.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Seyyasaka together with further information.
09-02.htm.intro:
Elder Seyyasaka was unable to maintain his chastity and broke the same rule again and again; when the Buddha was informed, he reminded him to keep the precepts and reproved him with a verse.
Keywords: Discontent, Masturbation, Restraint

09-03.htm.title: 9.3 The Story about the Devadhītā Lāja
09-03.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Devadhītā Lāja together with further information.
09-03.htm.intro:
A young woman working in the fields gave parched rice to Elder Mahā Kassapa and was thereby reborn as a Devadhītā in Tusita Heaven; she desired to do more good deeds for Elder Mahā Kassapa, but was restrained by him; the Buddha explained the reason for her motivation with a verse.
Keywords: Great Disciples, Offerings, Devadhītās, Death, Radiant Image

09-04.htm.title: 9.4 The Story about the Wealthy Anāthapiṇḍika
09-04.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Wealthy Anāthapiṇḍika together with further information.
09-04.htm.intro:
A Devatā in the house of Anāthapiṇḍika advised him to stop supporting the Buddha and his disciples as he was being brought to poverty; Anāthapiṇḍika reproved the Devatā and sent her out of his house; later she recovered the householder’s fortune and apologised; he took her to the Buddha who taught them both with some verses.
Keywords: Offerings, Poverty, Wealth, Rich Men, Devatās

09-05.htm.title: 9.5 The Story about a Bhikkhu Unrestrained with the Requisites
09-05.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about a Bhikkhu Unrestrained with the Requisites together with further information.
09-05.htm.intro:
A bhikkhu refused to look after his requisites, thinking them not worth the trouble; the Buddha told him he should not think in that way and admonished him with a verse.
Keywords: Requisites, Discipline

09-06.htm.title: 9.6 The Story about the Rich Man Biḷālapādaka
09-06.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Rich Man Biḷālapādaka together with further information.
09-06.htm.intro:
A wise man heard the Buddha teach on the merit of giving and encouraging giving, invited the Buddha and the Saṅgha for alms, and then requested others to help in the deed; the foolish merchant Biḷālapāda thought the man shouldn’t offer more than he can himself fulfil, and gave but little, but later feared he would be exposed for his stinginess; the wise man however praised all who gave, the fool repented and the Buddha gave a teaching in verse.
Keywords: Offerings, Rich Men, Misers, Merit

09-07.htm.title: 9.7 The Story about the Merchant Mahā Dhana
09-07.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Merchant Mahā Dhana together with further information.
09-07.htm.intro:
The merchant Mahā Dhana set out with five hundred wagons but learned there are thieves ahead and thieves behind, and so stayed put in a village; this was told to the Buddha who drew the lesson therefrom and spoke a verse.
Keywords: Thieves, Similes

09-08.htm.title: 9.8 The Story about Kukkuṭamitta
09-08.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Kukkuṭamitta together with further information.
09-08.htm.intro:
The Buddha taught Kukkuṭamitta the hunter, his seven sons and seven daughters, and they all gained Stream-entry; the Buddha also explained that the hunter’s wife attained Stream-entry while still young; the bhikkhus asked how can anyone who has Stream-entry help a hunter, and the Buddha explained the matter with a verse.
Keywords: Hunters, Conversions, Shrines, Rich Men, Merit, Past Lives, Previous Buddhas

09-09.htm.title: 9.9 The Story about the Hunter Koka’s Dogs
09-09.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Hunter Koka’s Dogs together with further information.
09-09.htm.intro:
The hunter Koka blamed a bhikkhu for his failure to catch game and he set his dogs on him, chasing him up a tree; the bhikkhu’s robe fell over the hunter and the dogs mistakenly devoured him instead; the bhikkhu worried whether his actions led to the death of the man, and the Buddha reassured him with a verse.
Keywords: Hunters, Animals, Past Lives

09-10.htm.title: 9.10 The Story about Elder Tissa, Who Frequented a Jeweller
09-10.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Elder Tissa, Who Frequented a Jeweller together with further information.
09-10.htm.intro:
Although Elder Tissa had received alms from a jeweller for a dozen years, when a heron swallowed a gem the jeweller accused Tissa of theft and started torturing him to get a confession; only when the heron was killed by accident did Elder Tissa reveal who took it, and he then passed away of his injuries; the Buddha explained the destiny of those involved with a verse.
Cast: Elder Tissa, King Pasenadi
Keywords: Thieves, Animals, Destinies

09-11.htm.title: 9.11 The Story about Three Groups
09-11.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Three Groups together with further information.
09-11.htm.intro:
Three different groups of bhikkhus who were on their way to the Buddha saw a crow die in mid-air, a woman drowned on a voyage and themselves get buried in a cave; they asked the Buddha why it all happened, and he explained there is nowhere to escape from the results of bad actions, and spoke a verse.
Keywords: Monastics, Death, Ships, Murder, Famines, Cruelty, Past Lives

09-12.htm.title: 9.12 The Story about Suppabuddha the Sākiyan
09-12.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Suppabuddha the Sākiyan together with further information.
09-12.htm.intro:
Suppabuddha the Sākiyan was the Buddha’s father-in-law, but was very arrogant and obstructed the Buddha when he was on almsround, which led to the Buddha predicting the time and place of his death; Suppabuddha thought he could escape his fate, but he met it anyway; then the Buddha spoke a verse explaining the matter.
Keywords: Arrogance, Destinies, Avīci

10-01.htm.title: 10.1 The Story about the Group of Six
10-01.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Group of Six together with further information.
10-01.htm.intro:
The Group of Six bhikkhus fought with and chased off the Group of Seventeen bhikkhus, and took their rooms; the Buddha laid down a rule against violence and spoke a verse.
Keywords: Golden Rule

10-02.htm.title: 10.2 The Story about the Group of Six
10-02.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Group of Six together with further information.
10-02.htm.intro:
The Group of six Bhikkhus fought with and chased off the Group of Seventeen bhikkhus, and took their rooms, which caused the latter to threaten them; the Buddha laid down a rule against threatening, and spoke a verse.
Keywords: Threats, Golden Rule

10-03.htm.title: 10.3 The Story about a Company of Boys
10-03.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about a Company of Boys together with further information.
10-03.htm.intro:
Some boys the Buddha met outside Sāvatthī were beating snakes, he advised them not to, as those who seek happiness for themselves should not hurt others.
Keywords: Golden Rule

10-04.htm.title: 10.4 The Story about the Elder Kuṇḍadhāna
10-04.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Kuṇḍadhāna together with further information.
10-04.htm.intro:
Elder Kuṇḍadhāna was followed round by a Devatā due to his behaviour in a previous existence, and the bhikkhus, thinking he was breaking his vow of chastity, incited the king to drive him out; the king believed in his innocence though and gave him an invitation; the bhikkhus blamed Elder Kuṇḍadhāna and he, unjustly, blamed them in return; the Buddha admonished him thus.
Cast: Kuṇḍadhāna, Buddha Kassapa
Keywords: Slander, Silence, Rich Men, Past Lives, Foremost Disciples, Previous Buddhas

10-05.htm.title: 10.5 The Story about Visākhā and Others Observing the Observance Days
10-05.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Visākhā and Others Observing the Observance Days together with further information.
10-05.htm.intro:
The great lay supporter Visākhā asked five hundred women why they observed the Observance Day; they answered they did so because they want a husband, children, release from their husbands or heaven; the Buddha explained that despite all their suffering most beings still only desire rebirth, and then he spoke a verse.
Keywords: Women, Aspirations, Great Disciples, Previous Buddhas

10-06.htm.title: 10.6 The Story about the Python Peta
10-06.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Python Peta together with further information.
10-06.htm.intro:
A leading supporter of the Buddha Kassapa recognised a thief as such, and the scoundrel conceived a grudge which led him to commit many wicked deeds, including burning his fields and burning down the Perfumed Cottage; he went to Niraya Hell and was later reborn in the world of the Petas where Elder Moggallāna saw him; the Buddha explained how he got there, and spoke a verse.
Cast: Elder Mahā Moggallāna, Elder Lakkhaṇa, Buddha Kassapa, Sumaṅgala
Keywords: Chief Disciples, Petas, Offerings, Merit, Forgiveness, Rich Men, Past Lives, Previous Buddhas

10-07.htm.title: 10.7 The Story about the Elder Mahā Moggallāna
10-07.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Mahā Moggallāna together with further information.
10-07.htm.intro:
Elder Moggallāna was murdered by brigands acting on behalf of the naked ascetics; the Buddha explained that in a past life, being swayed by his wife he had murdered his parents, which was why he died in this way in the present life, and then he spoke some verses.
Cast: Elder Mahā Moggallāna, King Ajātasattu
Keywords: Chief Disciples, Thieves, Killing, Past Lives

10-08.htm.title: 10.8 The Story about the Bhikkhu with Many Possessions
10-08.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Bhikkhu with Many Possessions together with further information.
10-08.htm.intro:
A householder went forth, but first had a cottage built for himself, with provisions stored up, slaves and many requisites so as to live comfortably; the bhikkhus complained to the Buddha who reproved the bhikkhu; in a tiff the bhikkhu threw off his robe and out of spite declared he would go around half-naked; the Buddha reproved him yet again with a verse.
Cast: Prince Mahiṁsāsa, Prince Canda, Prince Suriya, Vessavaṇa, Buddha Vipassī, King Bandhumati
Keywords: Requisites, Bodhisatta, Yakkhas, Past Lives

10-09.htm.title: 10.9 The Story about the Minister Santati
10-09.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Minister Santati together with further information.
10-09.htm.intro:
The minister Santati was given a rich reward by the king, including a dancing girl, but later she died; distressed, Santati went to the Buddha who gave him a teaching whereby he attained Nibbāna and soon after passed away still dressed in his finery; the bhikkhus asked whether he can be considered a Brahmin or an ascetic, and the Buddha confirmed his status with a verse.
Cast: Santati, King Pasenadi, Elder Ānanda, Buddha Vipassī, King Bandhumati
Keywords: Ministers, Dancing Girls, Grief, Merit, Relics, Past Lives

10-10.htm.title: 10.10 The Story about the Elder Pilotika
10-10.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Pilotika together with further information.
10-10.htm.intro:
The poor man Pilotika was ordained by Elder Ānanda, grew fat and discontented, and thought to return to the lay life; but finding his previous rags he took them as a meditation subject and soon became an Arahat; the Buddha confirmed his status to the bhikkhus and spoke some verses.
Keywords: Beggars, Monastics, Ordination

10-11.htm.title: 10.11 The Story about the Novice Sukha
10-11.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Novice Sukha together with further information.
10-11.htm.intro:
The novice Sukha saw that irrigators, fletchers and carpenters mastered the objects they worked with, and realised that, if they can master unconscious things, he could master his mind; he asked his teacher Elder Sāriputta to bring his food, and by striving alone he became an Arahat; the Buddha then spoke a verse about him.
Cast: Gandha, Bhattabhatika, Cintāmaṇī, Elder Sāriputta, Elder Sukha, Elder Paṇḍita, Sakka, Four Great Kings
Keywords: Offerings, Paccekabuddhas, Conversions, Novices, Rich Men, Great Disciples, Mastery, Past Lives

11-01.htm.title: 11.1 The Story about Visākhā’s Companions
11-01.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Visākhā’s Companions together with further information.
11-01.htm.intro: Women under the care of Visākhā partook of strong drink while on their way to listen to the Buddha; when they arrived they were possessed by Māra and started laughing and dancing; the Buddha, through his miraculous powers, sobered them up, and then spoke a verse.

11-02.htm.title: 11.2 The Story about Sirimā
11-02.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Sirimā together with further information.
11-02.htm.intro: Jīvaka’s sister Sirimā was a courtesan in Rājagaha who attained Stream-entry and used to provide alms for the bhikkhus, but soon she died; the Buddha asked for her body to be left outside to rot, and although men would pay good money for her before, nobody would take her later, even for free; the Buddha spoke about her in a verse.

11-03.htm.title: 11.3 The Story about the Elder Uttarī
11-03.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Uttarī together with further information.
11-03.htm.intro: The elderly bhikkhunī Uttarī still walked on almsround at the age of one hundred and twenty years; while walking one day she met the Buddha, but stumbled and fell down; the Buddha spoke a verse warning of her coming death.

11-04.htm.title: 11.4 The Story about Many Vain Bhikkhus
11-04.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Many Vain Bhikkhus together with further information.
11-04.htm.intro: Some bhikkhus attained absorption and thinking they had Awakened they went to see the Buddha; the Buddha sent them to the charnel ground, and when they saw female corpses they realised they still had lust; the Buddha then gave them this teaching.

11-05.htm.title: 11.5 The Story about the Elder Janapada Kaḷyāṇī Rūpanandā
11-05.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Janapada Kaḷyāṇī Rūpanandā together with further information.
11-05.htm.intro: The Buddha caused Elder Rūpanandā, who was proud of her beauty, to see an image of a very beautiful woman quickly go through the stages of life, die, and be eaten by animals, and she gained insight into the nature of the body; the Buddha then spoke a verse.

11-06.htm.title: 11.6 The Story about Queen Mallikā
11-06.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Queen Mallikā together with further information.
11-06.htm.intro: King Pasenadi’s wife Queen Mallikā died and was eventually reborn in Tusita Heaven; later the Buddha went on almsround, was invited by the king, and sat in his chariot hall, where he explained to the king that he shouldn’t grieve, for all beings must die, and there he spoke a verse.

11-07.htm.title: 11.7 The Story about the Elder Lāḷudāyi
11-07.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Lāḷudāyi together with further information.
11-07.htm.intro: The bhikkhu Lāḷudāyi was always reciting the wrong verses – dirges at weddings, and joyful verses at funerals, and so on; the Buddha explained that he did the very same in a past life and spoke a verse.

11-08.htm.title: 11.8 The Story about the Exalted Utterances (Spoken) to Elder Ānanda
11-08.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Exalted Utterances (Spoken) to Elder Ānanda together with further information.
11-08.htm.intro: After he had defeated Māra at the foot of the Bodhi tree, the Bodhisatta, in the three watches of the night, attained insight into his previous existences, the rising and falling away of beings according to their intentional actions, and dependent origination, which led to his Awakening, at which point he spoke exalted utterances.

11-09.htm.title: 11.9 The Story about Mahā Dhana, the Rich Man’s Son
11-09.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Mahā Dhana, the Rich Man’s Son together with further information.
11-09.htm.intro: The wealthy youth Mahā Dhana took to drink and squandered both his own and his wife’s money and ended up a beggar; the Buddha explained that if he had applied himself as a lay disciple he would have been amongst the chief rich men; and if he had gone forth he would have attained the paths and fruits; and then he spoke some verses about him.

12-01.htm.title: 12.1 The Story about Prince Bodhi
12-01.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Prince Bodhi together with further information.
12-01.htm.intro: Prince Bodhi invited the Buddha for the first meal in his new palace, and put down cloth thinking if the Buddha stepped on it he would be blessed with children; the Buddha refused to walk on it, and explained that Prince Bodhi would be without children because of a past life in which he failed to protect himself by keeping precepts during any of the three periods of his life, and he then gave a teaching in a verse.

12-02.htm.title: 12.2 The Story about the Elder Upananda the Sakyan
12-02.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Upananda the Sakyan together with further information.
12-02.htm.intro: Elder Upananda taught well, but was a greedy bhikkhu who always took the biggest offering, one day he swindled two bhikkhus out of a blanket, and the Buddha explained that one should train oneself before teaching to others, and summarised his teaching with a verse.

12-03.htm.title: 12.3 The Story about the Elder Padhānika Tissa
12-03.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Padhānika Tissa together with further information.
12-03.htm.intro: Elder Padhānika Tissa took five hundred bhikkhus with him and went to the forest; at night he urged them three times to put forth effort, but he himself went to sleep; the bhikkhus, being worn out, made no progress; the Buddha spoke a verse about the elder.

12-04.htm.title: 2.4 The Story about the Elder, the Mother of Kumāra Kassapa
12-04.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder, the Mother of Kumāra Kassapa together with further information.
12-04.htm.intro: A woman took ordination unaware that she was pregnant; when the child was born King Pasenadi offered to bring him up, and he became known as Kumāra Kassapa; later he ordained and became an Arahat; he also helped his mother give up her affection for him and attain insight; the Buddha then spoke a verse.

12-05.htm.title: 12.5 The Story about the Lay Disciple Mahā Kāla
12-05.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Lay Disciple Mahā Kāla together with further information.
12-05.htm.intro: The householder Mahā Kāla listened to an all-night Dhamma teaching at Jetavana, but in the morning was beaten to death by people who mistook him for a thief; the Buddha explained that he had caused the unjust death of another in a previous life, and his bad deed had caught up with him, and gave a teaching in a verse.

12-06.htm.title: 12.6 The Story about Devadatta
12-06.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Devadatta together with further information.
12-06.htm.intro: Devadatta sought to kill the Buddha and take over the running of the Saṅgha; the Buddha explained that he also tried to kill him in other existences, but it all worked to Devadatta’s downfall, and then he spoke a verse about him.

12-07.htm.title: 12.7 The Story about Trying for a Schism in the Saṅgha
12-07.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Trying for a Schism in the Saṅgha together with further information.
12-07.htm.intro: Devadatta informed Elder Ānanda that he would henceforth observe the Observance Day apart from the original Saṅgha, thereby causing a schism in the Saṅgha, the Buddha explained how easy it was for the bad to do bad, and then spoke a verse.

12-08.htm.title: 12.8 The Story about the Elder Kāla
12-08.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Kāla together with further information.
12-08.htm.intro: Elder Kāla was a good teacher but sought to prevent his supporter from listening to the Buddha, thinking she would abandon him; she went to listen anyway, and he followed her, thinking to persuade the Buddha not to teach deep teachings to her; the Buddha rebuked him and spoke a verse.

12-09.htm.title: 12.9 The Story about the Lay Disciple Culla Kāla
12-09.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Lay Disciple Culla Kāla together with further information.
12-09.htm.intro: The householder Culla Kāla listened to an all-night Dhamma teaching at Jetavana, but in the morning was beaten by people who mistook him for a thief; some courtesans interceded and they let him go; this was reported to the Buddha who gave the teaching in a verse.

12-10.htm.title: 12.10 The Story about the Elder Attadattha
12-10.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Attadattha together with further information.
12-10.htm.intro: When Elder Attadattha heard the Buddha declare his intention to finally pass away in four months time, rather than attend on the Buddha, he went to the forest to practice the teaching; the Buddha lauded him and said this is how one truly honours him, and spoke a verse.

13-01.htm.title: 13.1 The Story about a Certain Young Bhikkhu
13-01.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about a Certain Young Bhikkhu together with further information.
13-01.htm.intro: Visākhā’s granddaughter called a young bhikkhu a cut-head and he took offence at the insult; the Buddha first appeased him and then gave the teaching with a verse.

13-02.htm.title: 13.2 The Story about Suddhodana
13-02.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Suddhodana together with further information.
13-02.htm.intro: The Buddha returned to his home town, Kapilavatthu, and was received with great honour, but no one invited him for a meal, so the next day he went on almsround, which upset his father, the king, as being beneath his dignity; the Buddha explained that in the lineage of the Buddhas they always go on almsround, and then he spoke some verses.

13-03.htm.title: 13.3 The Story about 500 Bhikkhus with Insight
13-03.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about 500 Bhikkhus with Insight together with further information.
13-03.htm.intro: Five hundred bhikkhus were given a subject for meditation but did not attain, so they determined to return to the Buddha; on the way, they saw a mirage, and then bubbles bursting, and they realised the self had the same characteristics of impermanence; the Buddha then projected an image of himself and taught them with a verse.

13-04.htm.title: 13.4 The Story about Prince Abhaya
13-04.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Prince Abhaya together with further information.
13-04.htm.intro: Prince Abhaya was given a rich reward by the king, including a dancing girl, but later she died, and the prince went to the Buddha who gave him a teaching about how many times, in life after life, he had wept for this woman, and explained that only fools allow themselves to grieve, and then he spoke a verse.

13-05.htm.title: 13.5 The Story about the Elder Sammuñjani
13-05.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Sammuñjani together with further information.
13-05.htm.intro: Elder Sammuñjani spent all his time sweeping the monastery and never meditated, but Elder Revata admonished him to spend some time in meditation, which he did and he became an Arahat; the Buddha confirmed to the bhikkhu his attainment and spoke a verse.

13-06.htm.title: 13.6 The Story about the Elder Aṅgulimāla
13-06.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Elder Aṅgulimāla together with further information.
13-06.htm.intro: Aṅgulimāla was misled into killing many hundreds of people, but later met the Buddha who converted him and he soon became an Arahat; later he was recognised as the former killer and was stoned to death; the bhikkhus asked where he was reborn, and the Buddha explained he was not reborn at all, and spoke a verse about him.

13-07.htm.title: 13.7 The Story about the Weaver’s Daughter
13-07.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Weaver’s Daughter together with further information.
13-07.htm.intro: A weaver’s daughter heard the Buddha teach on contemplation of death and undertook the practice herself; after three years the Buddha returned to her home town and asked her four questions which she sagely answered, but no one understood her answers except the Buddha; he then spoke a verse, hearing which, she attained Stream-entry.

13-08.htm.title: 13.8 The Story about Thirty Bhikkhus
13-08.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Thirty Bhikkhus together with further information.
13-08.htm.intro: Elder Ānanda waited while thirty bhikkhus met with the Buddha, who brought them all the way to Arahatship, after which they flew away; seeing they were no longer there Elder Ānanda asked where they had gone and the Buddha explained they had left in the same way as the geese who they saw flying in the air at that moment.

13-09.htm.title: 13.9 The Story about the Young Brahmin Girl Ciñcā
13-09.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Young Brahmin Girl Ciñcā together with further information.
13-09.htm.intro: The young brahmin girl Ciñcā falsely accused the Buddha of impregnating her; the gods helped reveal the lie, and Ciñcā fell into Avīci, the hell of relentless suffering; the Buddha explained the matter with a verse.

13-10.htm.title: 13.10 The Story about the Gifts Beyond Compare
13-10.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about the Gifts Beyond Compare together with further information.
13-10.htm.intro: King Pasenadi gave Gifts Beyond Compare to the Saṅgha with the Buddha at its head, something which happens only once in a lifetime; one of the king’s ministers rejoiced, but another regretted the expenditure; the first was richly rewarded and the second was banished from the kingdom; the Buddha then spoke a verse about the situation.

13-11.htm.title: 13.11 The Story about Anāthapiṇḍika’s Son Kāla
13-11.htm.summary: high-definition creative commons posters telling The Story about Anāthapiṇḍika’s Son Kāla together with further information.
13-11.htm.intro: Anāthapiṇḍika had a son, who was interested in wealth, but not in listening to Dhamma; the householder therefore offered his son a thousand coins if he would go to the monastery, observe the Observance Day duties, and learn a verse from the Buddha; he did so and attained Stream-entry, and later refused his father’s money; the Buddha explained his decision with a verse.

Journey.title: The Journey to the West
Journey.summary:
high-definition creative commons posters based on Monkey by Arthur Waley (a translation of 30 out of 100 chapters of The Journey to the West by Cheng'en Wu), together with further information.
Source of the Stories
Journey.intro:
Born from a magic rock, the rebellious Monkey gains immortality and masters seventy-two transformations. After causing great havoc in Heaven, he is imprisoned under a mountain by Buddha for five hundred years. Released by the Bodhisattva Kuan-yin, he must protect the priest Tripitaka on a perilous pilgrimage to India. Joined by Pigsy and Sandy, they overcome immense supernatural dangers, retrieve the sacred scriptures, and finally achieve spiritual illumination in Paradise.
The pilgrimage is an allegorical journey toward spiritual enlightenment. Tripitaka represents the anxious, ordinary human, while Monkey symbolizes the restless, undisciplined mind. Alongside Pigsy (representing physical appetite) and Sandy (representing whole-hearted sincerity), they must conquer external obstacles to tame their inner desires. Shedding their earthly bodies and receiving blank scriptures teaches that ultimate truth lies in realizing the emptiness of all things.
There is a continuous rivalry between Buddhist and Taoists and Confucianists in the story (with the Buddhists winning, of course) but rather than eradicating the others after exposing its fraudulent leaders, showing a true Buddhist outlook, Monkey resolves the issue by establishing syncretic peace. He declares that the religions are one, and commands the king to reverence both Buddhist and other priests.

toc.label: 02 The Education of the Monkey King
